name: Sealing the Sense-Doors, Watching the Point Dissolve
previous_label: Parivrtta Trikonasana — Revolved Triangle (asana framing, retired 2026-10)

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: kararuddhadṛgastreṇa bhrūbhedād dvārarodhanāt | dṛṣṭe bindau kramāl līne tanmadhye paramā sthitiḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
dharana.rendering: Closing the doors [of the senses] with the hands used as a 'weapon' that blocks the eyes, and piercing [the point between] the eyebrows, a point of light (bindu) is seen; as it gradually dissolves, in its midst is the supreme state.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh describes the hand seal: thumbs close the ears, index fingers the eyes, middle fingers the nostrils, ring and little fingers the mouth, so that 'the vital energy is confined within'. Singh also reports that Swami Lakshmanjoo reverses the order: first concentrate on the brow until a drop of light appears, then apply the seal. Because the classical seal covers the eyes and closes the nose and mouth, this door is observe-only.
dharana.technique_name: Sealing the Sense-Doors, Watching the Point Dissolve

checked_against: GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y10 (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 36 does not prescribe a body position (it describes a hand seal over the senses, which this school does not teach). The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the sense openings of the head, closed by the hands
the bindu (point of light) and its dissolving
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the head with its sense-doors closed by the hands, a point at the brow, and a point of light that fades. The hand seal is part of the verse; this school does not teach it.
geometry.svg_hint: a head outline with hands over the face drawn faint, a small light point at the brow fading; observe-only
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Tangle to thread (observed)
reaction.summary: School metaphor: busy sense input narrows to one point of light that thins away. A picture for understanding, not a class exercise.

breath.lands_in: natural breath through the nose, never blocked
breath.cue: Natural breath only. No forced hold. Do not close the nostrils or mouth.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Study the verse; keep the face, eyes and brow soft
orientation.gravity: Fully supported; hands resting in the lap
orientation.gaze: Eyes open or gently closed without any pressure
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target; hands stay in the lap

attention.primary: Understanding the verse: senses closed, a point at the brow, a light that dissolves
attention.secondary: If sitting with it: soft attention at the brow with no pressure anywhere

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Closing the doors [of the senses] with the hands used as a 'weapon' that blocks the eyes, and piercing [the point between] the eyebrows, a point of light (bindu) is seen; as it gradually dissolves, in its midst is the supreme state.
adiyogi.method_summary: Classical method: a seal of the senses with the hands (covering the eyes and the other openings) while piercing attention at the eyebrow centre until an inner point of light appears and fades. Observe-only in this school: do not press the eyes or block the nostrils or mouth. The only class form is to rest soft attention at the brow with the hands in the lap and notice quiet.

honesty.disclosure: Door 013 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 13 (verse 36) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 013 is dharana 13, verse 36. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.
historical/observe_only: The classical hand seal covers the eyes and closes the nose and mouth. Taught as text to understand, not as a class drill.

legacy.disclosure: This [retired posture] and VBT method are paired by School of 112 Doorways index (Door 013 with dharana 013). That link is a teaching device, not a claim of ancient one-to-one canon.
legacy.notes: Experiential rhyme only: both ask attention toward a center line (spinal axis; brow point). Not justified as inner_logic or axis_pairing without stronger historical support.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Never press on the eyes or block the nose or mouth. Pressure on the eyeballs and obstruction of breathing are not taught by this school. Skip classical sensory-seal pressure on the eyes in class. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.open_seat_alternate: Hand on a block or the shin instead of the floor; shorten the stance; keep gaze down if the neck complains.
legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: General practice caution for deep twists, hamstrings, and neck. Not medical advice. Skip classical sensory-seal pressure on the eyes in class.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

safety.observe_only_note: Never press on the eyes or block the nose or mouth. Pressure on the eyeballs and obstruction of breathing are not taught by this school. Skip classical sensory-seal pressure on the eyes in class.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 013: sealing the sense-doors and watching the point dissolve. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 13, verse 36. This door is observe-only.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit comfortably with the hands resting in the lap. The verse uses the hands to close the senses; we do not.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Keep the face, eyes and brow soft. Eyes open or gently closed, with no pressure.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath through the nose. No forced hold. Nothing is blocked.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: If you sit with it, rest soft attention at the brow. Notice quiet. Nothing more.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: busy senses narrow to one point that thins away. A picture, not an exercise.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 36 seals the senses with the hands and watches a point of light dissolve at the brow. Observe-only here: do not press the eyes or plug the nostrils.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Open the eyes fully. Look around the room. Move on when ready.
